sections.heading: Common Roof Inspection Problems in Irvington, NJ

runs.v: comes from New Jersey's distinct seasonal shifts, which impact roofing materials: high winds tear away or crease asphalt shingles, ice dams form when melting snow refreezes at colder eaves, freeze-thaw cycles open cracks, severe weather can warp shingles, summer heat speeds granule loss, and shaded, humid slopes invite moss growth. Common roofing issues in New Jersey include leaks, worn materials, and drainage problems.

shapes an Irvington roof inspection: about 71% of occupied homes are rented and about 29% owner-occupied (U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019–2023), many in two- and three-family and investor-owned buildings, so entry is coordinated around occupants under New Jersey landlord-tenant notice.

fail together: heavy autumn leaf fall can overwhelm gutter systems and cause water damage, gutter overflow is common on two-family homes with undersized systems, and routine gutter maintenance prevents water backup and foundation damage. Finished attics, converted third-floor units, and drywalled-over hatches limit the interior view, so the inspector adds exterior detail where access is blocked.

turns up on Irvington's older homes: about 52% were built before 1960 and about 26% before 1940 (U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019–2023), and 1920s–1940s sheathing shows moisture decay a surface inspection misses. Inspectors check attic ventilation and insulation for energy efficiency against the NRCA and ARMA standard of 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor, because a ventilation imbalance can trap warm air, leading to mold growth and shingle damage.

sections.heading: Storm Damage, Roof Repair, or Replacement? The 25% Rule for Irvington Homes

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: When damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, replacement usually makes more sense than another repair; in New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months also requires a construction permit on any building other than a detached one- or two-family home, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. A roof in good shape may need only minor repairs to fix flashing or restore a seal.

, storm damage calls for a swift response: an active leak is triaged as an emergency, emergency tarping with temporary tarps gives emergency roof protection, and urgent storm damage repairs restore the roof. Asphalt shingles last about 20 years on average in Irvington, metal roofing 40–70 years depending on the material, and slate over 100 years with proper maintenance; EPDM is durable and flexible for flat roofs, and TPO is known for energy efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Proactive inspections extend the lifecycle of roofing materials and protect the investment, and when replacement is due, Newark Quality Roofing can install durable roofing systems as GAF-certified installers.

faqs.q: How often should an Irvington roof be inspected?

runs.v: At least twice a year, spring and fall, plus after any major weather event, per the NRCA; an inspection after a major storm is crucial. Regular inspections and maintenance services on that cadence extend asphalt-shingle service life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA.

faqs.q: Can a roof inspection find a leak before it appears inside an Irvington home?

runs.v: Yes. Moisture meters and infrared imaging find trapped moisture in the deck while the repair stays minor.
